pins.name: D13
pins.label: GPIO13 (Led active high)
pins.notes: PIN_LED (per pico-sdk's PICO_DEFAULT_LED_PIN) / Green user LED — onboard single status LED. Confirmed as the LED pin by THREE independent official sources: Melopero's own "Getting started" guide/product page ("Green user LED on pin 13"), Adafruit's compiled CircuitPython board port (MP_QSTR_LED -> pin_GPIO13), and the upstream Raspberry Pi pico-sdk board header (PICO_DEFAULT_LED_PIN 13). Polarity (active-high) is inferred, not directly source-quoted for this specific board: no dedicated Arduino/MicroPython library or Zephyr devicetree port exists for this board to cite a literal digitalWrite(13, HIGH)-turns-LED-on statement from (unlike the Cookie/Scorpio precedents), but pico-sdk's board header defines no PICO_DEFAULT_LED_PIN_INVERTED macro (which pico-sdk uses specifically to flag active-low boards, and does define on boards that need it), and every other RP2040 board audited in this repo so far has been confirmed active-high with no exceptions — both points converge on active-high. digital_input dropped to match this repo's established led_high precedent for dedicated onboard LED pins; pwm_output kept since arduino-pico's analogWrite() works on any RP2040 GPIO, enabling brightness dimming. NOTE: this board's own arduino-pico pins_arduino.h actually defines PIN_LED as GPIO25 (byte-for-byte identical to the generic Raspberry Pi Pico template's PIN_LED value) rather than GPIO13 — this is very likely un-updated boilerplate carried over from the generic Pico variant template when this board's core support was added (this board's pins_arduino.h is otherwise identical to the plain Pico template apart from Wire/SPI pin numbers), not a real second LED, since none of the three independent official sources above mention any function at all for GPIO25, and Melopero's own spec sheet names only one (singular) "Green user LED". See the GPIO25 NO CHANGE note below. Bus-alias collision: this board's pins_arduino.h originally also declared GPIO13 as PIN_SPI1_SS - fixed by removing that #define (see pins_arduino.h and its inline comment), since the official CircuitPython/pico-sdk board ports for this exact board document only one SPI bus (SPI0), confirming SPI1 is an unused/spare Feather-template default, matching the adafruit_feather_scorpio PIN_SPI0_SS precedent.

pins.name: D16
pins.label: GPIO16 (Led Neopixel)
pins.notes: PIN_NEOPIXEL (per pico-sdk's PICO_DEFAULT_WS2812_PIN) — onboard WS2812 addressable RGB LED, output-only data line. Confirmed via Melopero's own spec sheet ("RGB WS2812 LED (aka NeoPixel)"), Adafruit's compiled CircuitPython board port (MP_QSTR_NEOPIXEL -> pin_GPIO16), and the upstream pico-sdk board header (PICO_DEFAULT_WS2812_PIN 16) — three independent official sources all agree. digital_input/pwm_output omitted, matching this repo's established NeoPixel-tagging vocabulary (vccgnd_yd_rp2040 GPIO23, adafruit_feather_scorpio GPIO4, melopero_cookie_rp2040 GPIO17 precedents) — pwm_output is not meaningful for a bit-serial/PIO-driven WS2812 data line. No bus-alias collision: GPIO16 does not appear anywhere in this board's SPI0/SPI1/Wire0/Wire1/Serial1/Serial2 alias list.
